newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi stocks edge higher in quieter trading week.
newsitem.headline: Saudi stocks edge higher in quieter trading week.

text.p: Shares on the Saudi Arabian stock exchange crept higher in quieter trade last week, figures from the Riyadh-based Bakheet Financial Advisors (BFA) showed on Sunday.
The index moved up 0.69 percent to close at 149.44 points from the previous week's 148.42 points.
BFA said banking sector stocks dominated trade, accounting for 27 percent of trading volume of 3.35 million shares.
Services stocks made up 25 percent of turnover.
Trading value in the week fell to 634.97 million riyals ($169 million) from 1.6 billion riyals a week earlier.
Of the 60 companies traded, 27 rose, 18 slipped and 15 were unchanged.

The most active shares were Riyad Bank, which closed at 237 riyals from 241, Saudi Cement -- which ended a riyal lower at 184 riyals -- and Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC), which was flat at 406 riyals.
Among the top gainers in the week were Al-Jouf Agri, which ended 6.9 percent higher at 62 riyals.

SCECO-Central -- the Saudi Consolidated Electric Power Company for the central region -- firmed 6.1 percent to 87 riyals from 82, while SCECO-Western rose 5.2 percent to 81 riyals from 77 a week earlier.
Among the week's losers were Saudi Cable, which shed five riyals to 94 and Al-Ahsa Development, which was three percent weaker at 89 riyals. ($1=3.75 riyals)
